log.note:
T136 (A3) done. AUTHOR: agent-f401 (OpenCode); prep and implementation in this session (prep map: ui3-a3/PREP.md).

WHAT CHANGED. src/App.tsx: the split/unsplit ternary no longer changes the Writer's tree position -- ONE .split-panes > section.split-pane[data-side=left] renders in both modes (data-single on .split-panes when unsplit; the .writer.split-toolbar div and the SplitDivider + right pane render only in split mode), so opening or closing a split never remounts the left Writer. The shared toolbar div is a conditional sibling rendered BEFORE the stable .split-panes; renderWriter takes an inSplit flag: in split mode header/footer props are undefined and the fragment origin line renders as span.split-pane-origin inside that pane's .split-pane-header (left: title + origin; right: title + origin + close), and the fragment restore strip renders in .split-pane-footer under the pane's Writer (same Dropdown/restoreFragment wiring). src/components/split.css (new, imported by App.tsx): the [data-single] left-pane fill rule, .split-pane-origin, .split-pane-footer -- static layout only, no animations; existing styles.css split rules untouched. tests/split-view.spec.ts: four new cases (undo survives open; left scrollTop within 2 px across an open/close round trip; both panes' .ProseMirror tops equal within 1 px in continuous AND page view with a section left and fragment right; the footer page status follows the focused pane at once) plus the DOM-contract updates the stable wrapper requires: .split-pane-title queries scoped to .split-pane[data-side="right"] (the left pane now has a header too) and closed-split assertions assert no .split-pane[data-side="right"] (the left pane always exists).

ROOT CAUSE NOTE (for the reviewer): the first attempt keyed .split-panes across the ternary and still remounted -- a ternary whose branches are element vs fragment puts the same key in different key-spaces (fragment children get prefixed keys), so React replaced the node. DOM-identity probes (ui3-a3/probe-tmp/*.spec.mjs, logs in the probe run) proved the boundary: .editor-area survived, .split-panes was replaced; after the unconditional-wrapper restructure every node from .split-panes down to .ProseMirror keeps its identity across open/close.

ACCEPTANCE (plan PREVIEW(6)): npx tsc --noEmit -p . exit 0; fresh build exit 0 (build3.log); Playwright port 1675, workers 1, retries 0: tests/split-view.spec.ts --repeat-each=3 -> 42 passed, 0 failed (after-run6.log, report.json); the U13 reviewer probe -> 7 passed, 8 failed (probe-run3.log, probe-report.json) -- ALL EIGHT are the two mechanical DOM-contract patterns above, verified on P3 (unscoped .split-pane-title strict-mode violation) and P8 (.split-pane count 0 after close, now 1): NOT behaviour regressions; the deep data-safety cases that pass include split-safety Append-to-section (P1/P2 family, tests 274/305 green in the spec run). The probe files are the recorded U13 reviewer artifacts outside my registered paths: they need the same two-line contract updates (scope .split-pane-title to the right pane; closed-split means no .split-pane[data-side="right"]), which per the wave-2 U13-c2 precedent is a disclosed probe amendment -- coordinator/reviewer to rule on who applies it.

STOP RULE: tests/layout.spec.ts + tests/performance.spec.ts after the change -> 13 passed, 0 failed (layout-perf.log): the permanent wrapper changed no measurement.

DESIGN DOC: (for D2/T150) Split view: the left pane is a permanent .split-panes > .split-pane[data-side=left] structure (data-single when unsplit), so opening and closing a split never remounts or scrolls the left editor; both panes carry .split-pane-header when split (left: title and, for fragments, the origin line as .split-pane-origin; right: title, origin, close); a fragment pane shows its restore strip in .split-pane-footer.
